exposure: early postpartum depressive symptoms (measured by EPDS >= 10)
outcome: infant and toddler developmental milestones (fine motor, gross motor, language/communication, social/behavioral)
cohort: 574,282 children in Israel, attending Mother Child Healthcare Centers, whose mothers completed the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) postnatally and who underwent at least one developmental screening examination up to age 36 months.
finding: Children whose mothers had early postnatal depressive symptoms (EPDS >= 10) showed a higher rate of failure to complete age-appropriate developmental tasks across fine motor, gross motor, language/communication, and social/behavioral domains until three years of age.
